metal.title: Lead (Pb)
metal.dek: A non-essential heavy metal and pervasive environmental contaminant, and the one metal for which no agency has identified a safe level in children. This page states what each body has set, on what basis, and where the corpus supports it.

finding.title: Dietary nickel is a plant-staple accumulation trait
finding.dek: Six independent datasets spanning four decades and five jurisdictions converge on the same commodity ranking, which is the signature of an intrinsic plant trait rather than of localized contamination.

ingredient.title: Rice
ingredient.dek: The most-studied commodity in the corpus. Flooded cultivation mobilizes arsenic into a staple crop, which is why rice carries matrix-specific limits that other cereals do not.

regulation.title: FDA Closer to Zero
regulation.dek: The FDA program for reducing dietary exposure to lead, arsenic, cadmium, and mercury in foods eaten by babies and young children. Action levels here are nonbinding guidance, not statutory maximum levels.

metalsIdx.title: Metals
metalsIdx.dek: Per-metal reference pages covering toxicology, exposure routes, food sources, and regulatory limits, with an at-a-glance comparison and the species distinctions that govern them.

productsIdx.title: Product categories
productsIdx.dek: Heavy-metal evidence for consumer food and personal-care product categories, organized by category and subcategory.

regulationsIdx.title: Regulations
regulationsIdx.dek: Regulatory thresholds, action levels, and guidance on heavy metals in food across jurisdictions.

source.title: Scientific Opinion on Lead in Food
source.dek: EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain, 2010. The opinion that withdrew the tolerable weekly intake for lead and reported benchmark dose lower confidence limits for three endpoints.

synthesis.title: Synthesis findings
synthesis.dek: Conclusions the corpus supports across independent sources, each graded for the strength of that support and published alongside the evidence that argues against it.

portal.title: Product categories
portal.dek: Consumer-facing categories, grouped by how a person encounters them. A portal is navigation: it states what exists, how much of it has been reviewed, and where the evidence lives.

category.title: Infant and child foods
category.dek: Thirty-eight categories consumed by the population with the highest intake per unit body weight in the food supply. Four metals govern the group; the subcategories differ in which one dominates.

browse.title: Search the Index
browse.dek: Records across metals, ingredients, product categories, regulations, and the source archive, ranked by the depth of evidence routed to each.
